subject: Hakeem Jeffries speaker nomination
title: Is Hakeem Jeffries speaker? Democrats nominate him; House votes Jan. 3
answer: Not yet. On Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, House Democrats nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York for speaker in a closed-door vote in which he ran unopposed. The full House will elect the speaker when the new Congress convenes on Jan. 3, 2027. If he wins, he will be the first Black speaker in U.S. history.
in_the_news: Democrats won back the House in the Nov. 3 midterms with one of their largest majorities in decades, so their nominee is all but certain to get the gavel. Wednesday's vote also set the rest of the new majority's leadership team.
body:
Jeffries, who has led House Democrats since January 2023, asked for a counted vote rather than approval by acclamation, the same approach Democrats used in their 2018 leadership elections, CBS News reported. No one stepped forward to challenge him. Two other unopposed picks made history of their own: Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts is in line to be the first woman to serve as majority leader, and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California the first Latino majority whip, PBS NewsHour reported.

The nomination was smooth, but the caucus is restless. Some incoming progressives declined to back Jeffries or held off to learn where he stands on their priorities, and protesters heckled him at a Democratic gathering in Denver the week before. Supporters including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York said he was effectively the only candidate. With Democrats on track for more than 250 seats, well above the 218 needed for a majority, a handful of holdouts has far less leverage than dissenters had in recent Republican-run Houses.

The road to Jan. 3, step by step: On Nov. 3, voters handed Democrats a House majority; Fox 5 New York counted a pickup of 42 seats as of Nov. 17. On Nov. 10, House Republicans chose Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio as their leader in the minority, beating Rep. Steve Scalise of Louisiana 106-73, after Speaker Mike Johnson said he would step aside from leadership. On Nov. 18, Democrats nominated Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar. In early December, Senate Democrats hold their own leadership vote, where Sen. Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland. On Jan. 3, the full House votes by roll call, with each member calling out a name, and the winner needs a majority of the members who vote for a candidate.

Until then, Johnson remains speaker of the current House. The floor vote is usually a formality for the majority party's nominee, but it has not always been: in January 2023, Republican Kevin McCarthy needed 15 rounds of voting before he won.

faq.a: A Democrat who represents a Brooklyn-based district in New York and has been the House Democratic leader since January 2023, when he succeeded Nancy Pelosi as head of the caucus.

faq.q: When will Jeffries officially become speaker?
faq.a: The House elects its speaker on Jan. 3, 2027, the day the new Congress convenes. He takes the gavel only after winning that floor vote.
Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio. Republicans elected him minority leader on Nov. 10, 2026, and Mike Johnson is leaving GOP leadership when the new Congress begins.

faq.q: Why do some progressives hesitate to back Jeffries?
faq.a: Some newly elected members want to hear where he stands on the policies they campaigned on before committing. None ran against him in Wednesday's caucus vote.
